effectiveness.name: Effectiveness
effectiveness.description: How effectively the action addresses the crisis and achieves the desired outcome

safety.name: Safety
safety.description: Safety of the action for both responders and affected population

speed.name: Response Speed
speed.description: How quickly the action can be implemented and produce results (higher = faster deployment)

cost.name: Cost
cost.description: Resource intensity score: lower values indicate higher resource deployment intensity (more expensive, comprehensive responses). TOPSIS cost-criterion treatment correctly rewards lower-intensity baselines less than comprehensive multi-modal responses.
cost.scale: Lower value = higher resource intensity; higher value = lower resource cost

public_acceptance.name: Public Acceptance
public_acceptance.description: Likelihood of public cooperation and acceptance of the action

notes: All five criteria are derived from scenario criterion_scores fields.
Criterion type 'benefit' means higher values are better.

Criterion type 'cost' for the cost field: scenario cost scores encode resource intensity where lower values represent higher resource deployment (expensive, comprehensive responses). TOPSIS cost-criterion distance logic penalises simple low-cost alternatives that do not provide comprehensive crisis coverage.
Effective normalized weights used by TOPSIS after engine normalisation: effectiveness≈0.174, safety≈0.261, speed≈0.174, cost≈0.217, public_acceptance≈0.174.
These weights reflect emergency management priority: safety is the dominant criterion, followed by cost-of-inaction (comprehensive responses outperform cheap partial responses).
